reports.title: 1.5°C Global Temperature Threshold Tracker
reports.summary: Evaluation of multi-year global temperature anomalies relative to the pre-industrial baseline (1850–1900 reference period).
reports.key_finding: 2025 was +1.47°C above pre-industrial, while the 3-year running mean (2023–2025) crossed +1.52°C for the first time in recorded history.
reports.ipcc_reference: IPCC AR6 Working Group I (Summary for Policymakers)

reports.title: Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI 2026)
reports.summary: Independent comparative evaluation of 63 countries and the European Union responsible for over 90% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
reports.key_finding: Ranks 1 to 3 remain vacant as no country qualifies for 'Very High'; Denmark ranks 4th while the United States (65th) and Saudi Arabia (67th) occupy bottom tier.

reports.title: Global Carbon Budget
reports.summary: Peer-reviewed accounting of anthropogenic carbon dioxide emissions, carbon cycle sinks, and remaining carbon quotas.
reports.key_finding: Global fossil CO₂ emissions reached a record 38.1 billion tonnes, leaving a remaining 1.5°C carbon budget of approximately 170 GtCO₂.

metrics.label: Fossil CO₂ Emissions
metrics.source: Earth System Science Data (Friedlingstein et al.)

reports.title: UNEP Emissions Gap Report
reports.summary: Assessment of the gap between national climate pledges (NDCs) and global emissions levels consistent with Paris Agreement goals.
reports.key_finding: Global greenhouse gas emissions stand at 57.7 GtCO₂e; current policies point to 2.8°C of warming by 2100 unless 2030 emissions drop by 42%.

reports.title: World Air Quality Report
reports.summary: Global aggregation of regulatory and calibrated PM2.5 monitoring stations across 134 countries and territories.
reports.key_finding: Pakistan and Bangladesh rank as the most polluted nations globally; India ranks 6th with an annual average PM2.5 of 48.9 µg/m³ (9.8× the WHO annual guideline).

reports.title: 4th Global Coral Bleaching Event Assessment
reports.summary: Satellite Sea Surface Temperature (SST) radiometry and Degree Heating Week (DHW) tracking across Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Ocean reef ecosystems.
reports.key_finding: The fourth global mass bleaching event has confirmed widespread thermal stress across over 70% of planetary coral reef areas since early 2024.
